clauses.reason: The only command is: "I hereby further exempt the said Lawrence M. Lawson from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1953." The order fixes the length of the further exemption, so it ended by its own terms with that period. January 31, 1953 is recorded inclusive, with the exclusive reading (ends as January 31 begins) as the alternative. No held order revokes or extends it, so this is the first end. State on 2026-10-14: terminated.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory records this clause as the word run of the stated period only. The operative command is the sentence that begins 'NOW, THEREFORE' and ends 'January 31, 1953.'; the single WHEREAS paragraph is a recital that recites the earlier three-year exemption under Executive Order No. 10002 of September 17, 1948.

research_rationale:
EO 10320 (17 FR 693; signed January 21, 1952) further exempts Lawrence M. Lawson, Commissioner of the United States on the International Boundary and Water Commission, United States and Mexico, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1953." The recital says he had been exempted for three years by Executive Order No. 10002 of September 17, 1948; that earlier order is a prior instrument, not a later event. The first end is the own-terms date January 31, 1953, recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through that day), with the exclusive reading (ends as January 31 begins) as the alternative. The quotation is from the Federal Register text layer held for this order, a government printed copy.
